title: Bellarmine: Paul taught when Antichrist would come — Augustine says we cannot know it
source_text: XVII. Sed instat Bellarminus, non omnia quae Apostolus docuit scriptis postea fuisse comprehensa. Nam, inquit, Apostolus in hoc ipso capite indicat se docuisse Thessalonicenses quando Antichristus venturus esset, & quid adventum ejus moraretur. Et nunc, inquit, quid detineat scitis. Et nunc retinet, quia quum essem apud vos, haec dicebam vobis. Hoc autem nusquam scriptum est, quando, scilicet, sit venturus Antichristus. Quare beatus Augustinus lib. 20. de Civit. Dei, dicit illos scivisse quod Apostolus docuerat viva voce, nos autem non posse id scire qui Apostolum non audivimus. Ergo non omnia scripta sunt quae Apostolus dixit.
pass_a_gloss: But Bellarmine presses that not all things which the Apostle taught were afterward comprehended in writings. For, he says, the Apostle in this very chapter indicates that he taught the Thessalonians when the Antichrist would come, and what would delay his coming. And now, he says, you know what restrains. And now he restrains, because when I was with you, I told you these things. But this is nowhere written, namely when the Antichrist is to come. Wherefore blessed Augustine in book 20 of the City of God says that they knew what the Apostle had taught by living voice, but that we who have not heard the Apostle cannot know it. Therefore not all things are written which the Apostle said.
pass_b_english: Bellarmine's press: not everything Paul taught later landed in writing.
2 Thess: you know what restrains — he had said these things when present.
The calendar of Antichrist's coming is nowhere written.
Augustine Civ. Dei 20: hearers knew by living voice; we who did not hear cannot know that point.

lemmas.gloss: book 20 of the City of God
